title: He Went To Prison For A Crime He Never Did . . . Then His Daughter Walked In
caption:
Miracle in Cell No. 7 (2013): a simple, loving father is framed for the death of the police chief's daughter, and his little girl is smuggled into his prison cell. Can the truth ever clear his name?

#miracleincellno7 #koreanmovie #movierecap #kmovie #spoilerroom
comment: Would you have signed the confession to protect your child? Why?

segments.say: A guard drags a father away from his little girl, and she screams for him through the *bars*.

segments.text: Don't cry, dad. Don't say save me.

segments.say: To see how it got here, go back to a toy *store*.
Sam is a simple man with the heart of a child, and Lily is his whole *world*.
She wants one thing, a Sailor Moon *bag*, but they can't afford it.
Then a rich man's wife grabs the last one, and the two dads start *shoving*.
Sam promises Lily he will get her that bag. The next day he goes back to *work*.
That's when he spots a girl wearing the exact same *bag*.
He chases after her, but she slips and hits her *head*.
Sam does the only thing he knows. He starts pressing on her *chest*.
Then her mother sees a stranger on top of her daughter and screams *kidnapper*.
The girl, Amy, was the police chief's *daughter*.
He is a powerful man, and he wants someone to *pay*.
So the cops beat Sam until he signs a confession for a crime he never *committed*.
Sam never stood a chance.
Meanwhile Lily sits alone at home, watching the clock and waiting for her *dad*.
They drag Sam through a screaming mob for a crime scene *reenactment*.
Lily runs after the police van, crying out for her *father*.
Sam ends up in Cell Seven, with five hardened *criminals*.
When they hear what he's accused of, they go for his *throat*.
But it doesn't take long to see the truth. This man couldn't hurt a *fly*.
These killers turned out softer than the cops.
Underneath the tattoos, they are just fathers who miss their *kids*.
So when Sam cries for his daughter, the cell makes a *plan*.
A prisoner wheels a big box past the guards, and nobody looks *inside*.
Inside the box, curled up asleep, is *Lily*.
Sam holds his girl and can't stop *sobbing*.
Now six men have to hide a little girl from the *guards*.
They feed her, dress her, and teach her to *laugh* again.
Lily draws pictures on the walls, and Sam learns to write her *name*.
Then the head guard, Hale, catches them at *night*.
He yells at the whole cell, and they stand in a line with their hands up, saying *nothing*.
Then a fire tears through the block, and Hale goes down in the *smoke*.
Sam runs straight into the flames and starts pressing on Hale's *chest*.
Hale wakes up in the hospital and learns who saved his *life*.
Now Hale owed Sam everything.
So he looks the other way, and Lily starts *school*.
Every day she comes home to her father in a prison *cell*.
At night she falls asleep in his arms, and for a little while the prison feels like *home*.
But the police chief never *forgets*.
He sends a prosecutor to Sam with a simple *threat*.
Confess, or the chief will go after your *daughter*.
So to protect Lily, Sam signs the *confession*.
He gave up his whole life for her.
In court the judge asks if he did it. Sam looks down and says *yes*.
Lily watches from the crowd, not understanding why her dad is *lying*.
The judge doesn't blink. Sam is sentenced to *death*.
The cellmates and Hale know time is short, so they plan one wild last day for Sam and Lily.
They sneak her into the yard, and Sam and Lily float up over the prison walls in a *balloon*.
Sam grins from the basket, and for a few minutes the whole prison forgets where it *is*.
On Lily's birthday, they share a bowl of seaweed soup, laughing like nothing is *wrong*.
But the next morning, the guards come for *Sam*.
Lily grabs the bars and begs them to *stop*.
Sam holds his little girl one last time and tells her not to *cry*.
Years later, Lily is a lawyer, standing in the same *court*.
She proves the old statements were forged, and Sam never touched *Amy*.
The court finally clears his *name*.
Too late for Sam, but not too late for the truth.
And in the snow, Lily looks up at the sky and remembers the day they *flew*.
